title: Genuina principia doctrinae de statu aequilibrii et motu corporum tam perfecte flesibilium quam elasticorum

deep.reconstruction:
This is the last page of §XLIII of E410. Euler specialises his general planar equations for a flexible or elastic line to small transverse vibrations of a lamina. The setting from the previous page is: the angle Φ between tangent and axis is near 90°, x ≈ s, dΦ/ds = −y'', and there are no distributed loads P and Q. In that case the normal (shear) force is V = −S'y'' − S y''', where S(s) is the bending stiffness. The tangential and normal balance laws are T' − V y'' = 0 and V' + T y'' = (Σ/2g) y_tt, where Σ is the line density and g the gravity constant of his units.

On this page Euler takes a uniform lamina, S = A, so V = −A y'''. Substituting into the tangential equation gives dT/ds = −A y'' y'''. Multiplying by ds and integrating gives T = B − (A/2)(y'')², with B a constant tension. Inserting V and T into the normal equation gives
−A y'''' + [B − (A/2) y''²] y'' = (Σ/2g) y_tt.
This is a fourth-order equation. Linearised, it is A y'''' − B y'' + (Σ/2g) y_tt = 0, the beam under axial tension (the 'stiff string'). With B = 0 it is the Euler–Bernoulli vibrating-beam equation. Euler only says one 'arrives at a differential equation of the fourth degree, as those who treated this subject more fully also found'. He does not write the equation out. The purpose is to show that his new general principles (with shear force V explicitly present) reproduce the known string and lamina vibration equations as special cases. The relation T + (A/2)κ² = const is the planar form of the classical first integral of the elastica / Kirchhoff rod equations.
errors: There is an order-of-smallness inconsistency. Under the stated linearisation (sin Φ = 1, dx/dt = 0), T' = −A y''y''' is of second order. Consistently T should simply be constant, as in the string case on p. 412. Keeping the (A/2)y''² correction while dropping tangential inertia and other geometric nonlinearities gives a non-systematic cubic term (A/2)(y'')³ if one does not linearise. Euler does not discuss this and does not write the final equation.
The final fourth-order equation is only asserted, not displayed. The reader must perform the elimination. The result with general B (axial tension) is not stated explicitly.

ideas.what: Shear force in a uniform beam equals minus stiffness times the third derivative of deflection (V = −A y''')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1730s–1740s); clean force-balance treatment of shear credited by Truesdell to Euler's E410 (1771)
ideas.where_published: E410 itself (Novi Comm. Petrop. 15, 1771); earlier beam vibration work by Euler (e.g. E65 Additamentum I, 1744) and in Euler–D. Bernoulli correspondence; discussed by Truesdell, Opera omnia II-11/2

ideas.what: Integration of T' = −A κ κ' to T + (A/2)κ² = const
ideas.modern_name: First integral of the planar elastica / Kirchhoff rod equations (tension plus half bending energy density constant)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Euler's elastica (1744); Kirchhoff (1859) for rods generally
ideas.where_published: Appears here in E410; whether Euler states it elsewhere in this form is unsure

ideas.what: Fourth-order equation for transverse vibration of a lamina, including a constant tension B
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Bernoulli beam equation / stiff-string (beam under tension) equation A w'''' − B w'' + ρ w_tt = 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Daniel Bernoulli and Euler (1735–1744) for the beam; the stiff string is often associated with later acoustics (Seebeck, Rayleigh) though implicit earlier
ideas.where_published: Euler E65 (Methodus inveniendi, Additamentum I), E40/E126-era papers on lamina vibration; recovered as a special case in E410

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine consistency check: the general 1771 equations reproduce the known fourth-order lamina equation. The only mildly notable points are the explicit first integral T = B − (A/2)y''² and an implicit tension term giving the stiff-string equation. Both are well known and E410 is extensively analysed by Truesdell.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially correct. The page ends with the catchword 'DE' (start of next item), not further text of E410.
'peruenitur' and 'inuenerunt', 'tractauerunt' use the u-for-v orthography of the original; correct as printed.
